1	# PRD: Viva, an AI interview coach for the AI-coding era
2	
3	Status: v2 for the DEV Hacktoberfest 2026 Weekend Challenge (Build for a Friend)
4	Owner: Abdul Wasih
5	Deadline: Mon 5 Oct 2026, 12:29 PM IST
6	
7	## 1. Problem
8	
9	Final-year students put one or two projects on their resume. In placement interviews and project vivas, the panel opens with "walk me through your project", then quickly asks "why did you choose X?", "what happens if Y fails?", "how would this scale?".
10	
11	Two things make this harder now:
12	1. Many students have never been questioned on their project. They freeze, give vague answers, or discover gaps live in the interview.
13	2. More and more of each project is written by AI coding agents. Interviewers know it and probe exactly those parts. A student who cannot explain code their agent wrote looks worse than one who wrote less.
14	
15	Generic interview prep tools ask generic questions. Nothing questions you about *your* code, and nothing knows which parts your AI wrote.
16	
17	## 2. The friend
18	
19	[FRIEND_NAME] is Wasih's batchmate. Their project is [FRIEND_PROJECT] (one line). Placements are coming up. In a recent mock or real interview they [one true moment where they froze]. [Optional: how much of the project was AI-assisted, in their words.] Viva is built for them first.
20	
21	Success for the friend: after two sessions they can answer "why" and "what if" questions about their own project with confidence, understand the parts their AI wrote, and know which 3 to 5 topics to revise.
22	
23	(Fill in with real facts before Phase 9. This is the opening of the DEV post.)
24	
25	## 3. Why open models (the challenge's core question)
26	
27	- **Privacy:** in local mode, code (including private repos), answers, and memory never leave the laptop. The hosted demo stores nothing.
28	- **Free forever:** practice 50 times the night before an interview, no bill.
29	- **Offline:** local folder + Ollama + Gemma works with Wi-Fi off, for example in a college lab. Shown live in the demo.
30	- **Control and ownership:** prompts, rubric, personas, and model are all swappable. Any coding club can deploy its own private Viva on Render in one click, running Gemma on its own instance.
31	- **Honest trade-offs:** voice mode sends audio to ElevenLabs; say so in the post and keep text mode fully private.
32	
33	Gemma is the brain: it reads the project, decides what to ask, judges answers, and writes the report. Mastra (open source) runs the agent loop.
34	
35	## 4. Users and scenarios
36	
37	1. **Student prepping for placements** (primary): pastes their repo, does a 15-minute interview (voice or text), reads the report, revises, comes back; Viva retests last time's weak spots.
38	2. **Student who leaned on an AI agent:** their repo has Entire checkpoints; Viva targets the AI-written parts.
39	3. **Student with a private repo:** runs Viva locally on a folder with local Gemma.
40	4. **Coding club lead:** clicks "Deploy to Render" to host a private Viva for the club.
41	5. **Judge / visitor:** opens the hosted link, clicks a sample repo, finishes a short interview in about 2 minutes.
42	
43	## 5. Scope
44	
45	### Must have
46	
47	- **F1. Project ingestion**
48	  - Input: public GitHub URL; local mode also accepts a folder path.
49	  - Select the most informative files: README, manifests, architecture-revealing configs (docker-compose, schemas, env examples), entry points, central source files. Skip lockfiles, binaries, build output, vendored code.
50	  - Token budget sized to the local ~4B Gemma context (measured in Phase 0).
51	  - Gemma produces a **ProjectBrief**: summary, stack, components, visible design decisions, risks, and interview "hooks" (specific files, functions, choices).
52	  - **Every path in the brief is validated against the real file list; invented paths are dropped and counted** (this count is a Sentry metric).
53	  - The user reviews the brief and can add one correction ("the frontend was my teammate's").
54	
55	- **F2. AI provenance from Entire (standout feature)**
56	  - If the repo contains Entire checkpoints, read them: which commits and files were agent-assisted, and the prompt that started each piece.
57	  - Build an **AI-authored map** (file, approximate scope, originating prompt summary). Use Entire's attribution data if available; otherwise use commit-level file lists.
58	  - Add hooks of kind `ai-authored`; the interviewer must ask at least one question about AI-written code and may quote the original prompt ("your session asked the agent to 'add JWT auth'. Walk me through how the refresh works").
59	  - Show an "AI-written areas" panel on the brief screen.
60	  - No checkpoints present: skip quietly, with a hint about Entire.
61	  - Local mode reads via git (or the Entire CLI); hosted mode via the GitHub API on public repos.
62	
63	- **F3. Interviewer agent (Mastra)**
64	  - A Mastra agent with tools:
65	    - `listFiles`, `readFile(path, range?)`: open more code mid-interview for a sharper deep-dive question (validated paths only)
66	    - `getProvenance(path)`: was this AI-written, and from what prompt
67	    - `recallWeakSpots(repoId)` / `saveWeakSpots(repoId, items)`: cross-session memory
68	  - Rounds: Overview, Decisions, Deep dive (incl. AI-written code), Failure and scale, Wrap-up.
69	  - Default 8 main questions (5 to 12), max 2 follow-ups each.
70	  - Each turn: evaluate the last answer against the rubric, decide follow-up or move on, ask the next question.
71	  - **Follow-ups must reference the candidate's actual answer.** Main quality bar.
72	  - "Skip" and "I don't know" are scored and added to the revision list.
73	  - Personas: **Friendly HR round** and **Tough tech lead**; each has its own instructions and voice.
74	
75	- **F4. Memory across sessions (Mastra memory, local mode)**
76	  - At the end of an interview, save weak spots and missed rubric points per repo.
77	  - Next session on the same repo opens with: "Last time you struggled with X. Let's start there." and retests them.
78	  - Report shows progress vs last session (score change per topic).
79	  - Stored on the laptop only; a "forget this project" button clears it. Hosted mode: memory off, labeled as a local-mode feature.
80	
81	- **F5. Voice and delivery coaching (ElevenLabs)**
82	  - TTS for interviewer questions, a different voice per persona.
83	  - STT for spoken answers, with word-level timestamps; transcript editable before sending.
84	  - **Delivery metrics** computed in code from timestamps and transcript: filler-word count and rate ("umm", "uh", "basically", "like", "actually"), long pauses (over 2 s), speaking pace (words per minute), answer length.
85	  - Report section "How you said it" next to "What you said", with simple targets (for example, pace 120 to 160 wpm).
86	  - Text mode stays default fallback when mic or keys are missing.
87	
88	- **F6. Report**
89	  - Per question: question, answer summary, score 0 to 4, good points, missing points, flagged if about AI-written code.
90	  - Overall: readiness, strengths, top 3 to 5 weak spots, revision list, 5 likely next questions, delivery summary, progress vs last session.
91	  - Export Markdown.
92	
93	- **F7. Two modes, one codebase**
94	  - **Local:** Ollama + ~4B Gemma, folders, memory, offline capable.
95	  - **Hosted (Render):** web service plus a private Ollama + Gemma service on Render; fallback to a hosted Gemma endpoint. GitHub URLs only, per-IP rate limit, sample repos with cached briefs.
96	  - **Deploy to Render** button with `render.yaml` blueprint in the README.
97	
98	- **F8. Agent tracing (Sentry)**
99	  - Every agent step and model call traced: operation, model, provider, latency, tokens, tool calls.
100	  - Custom quality attributes: `invented_paths_dropped`, `json_repair_used`, `followup_references_answer` (judged cheaply in code or by a short check), `question_names_real_file`, `ai_authored_question`.
101	  - A Sentry dashboard of these metrics; comparison of local ~4B vs hosted larger Gemma.
102	  - No answer text or audio in traces (metadata only).
103	  - One real debugging story found via traces.
104	
105	- **F9. Text interview UI**
106	  - Start: repo input, mode badge (Local, private / Hosted demo), persona, length, target role, voice toggle, sample repos.
107	  - Brief review: summary, stack, hooks, AI-written areas, "last time" weak spots, correction box.
108	  - Interview: chat layout, round label, progress, answer box, mic button, skip, end early, status text ("reading src/auth.ts...") when the agent uses tools.
109	  - Report screen.
110	
111	### Nice to have (first to cut)
112	
113	- If the chosen Gemma accepts images: ask about the architecture diagram in the candidate's README.
114	- Difficulty slider beyond the two personas.
115	- Mobile polish.
116	
117	### Out of scope
118	
119	Accounts, server-side databases, private repos in hosted mode, video, proctoring, resume parsing.
120	
121	## 6. Functional details
122	
123	### Schemas (zod, `src/lib/interview/schemas.ts`)
124	
125	- `ProjectBrief`: summary, stack[], components[{name, purpose, files[]}], decisions[], risks[], hooks[{id, kind: "file"|"function"|"decision"|"risk"|"ai-authored", ref, why}]
126	- `ProvenanceEntry`: path, commit, checkpointId, promptSummary, scope ("file"|"lines"), lines?
127	- `Question`: id, round, persona, text, hookId?, filesRead[], rubric{mustMention[], goodSignals[], redFlags[]}, isFollowUp, parentId?, aboutAiCode
128	- `Evaluation`: questionId, answerSummary, score 0 to 4, good[], missing[], followUp{ask, reason}
129	- `DeliveryMetrics`: durationSec, words, wpm, fillerCount, fillerRate, longPauses[], fillersByWord{}
130	- `WeakSpot`: topic, evidence, lastScore, sessionDate
131	- `InterviewState`: brief, provenance[], userCorrection?, previousWeakSpots[], questions[], answers[], evaluations[], delivery[], round, counts, settings
132	- `Report`: overall, readiness, perQuestion[], strengths[], weakSpots[], revisionList[], likelyNextQuestions[], deliverySummary, progressVsLast[]
133	
134	### API
135	
136	- `POST /api/ingest` returns `{ brief, provenance, filesUsed, previousWeakSpots }`
137	- `POST /api/turn` `{ state, answer, delivery? }` returns `{ state, evaluation?, nextQuestion | done, toolActivity[] }`
138	- `POST /api/report` `{ state }` returns `{ report }` (and saves weak spots in local mode)
139	- `POST /api/tts` `{ text, persona }` returns audio
140	- `POST /api/stt` audio returns `{ transcript, words[{text,start,end}], delivery }`
141	
142	State travels with the client; the server is stateless except local-mode memory.
143	
144	### Scoring rubric (0 to 4)
145	
146	0 no answer or wrong; 1 vague, not specific; 2 correct but shallow; 3 solid and specific; 4 excellent, with trade-offs or alternatives.
147	
148	## 7. Non-functional requirements
149	
150	- Latency: under 8 s per turn hosted; local measured and reported honestly.
151	- Robustness: bad model output never crashes the UI.
152	- Privacy: no server persistence in hosted mode; memory local only; no answer text or audio in traces or logs.
153	- Cost: hosted demo within free tiers and partner credits; rate limited.
154	- Explainability: readable by a final-year student; prompts in one place.
155	
156	## 8. Success metrics (measured; real numbers go in the post)
157	
158	- Structured output validity after repair: 95%+
159	- Follow-ups referencing the actual answer: 8 of 10 in a manual check
160	- Deep-dive questions naming a real file: 80%+
161	- Invented paths reaching the user: 0 (all caught by validation; report how many were caught)
162	- On a repo with checkpoints, at least 1 AI-authored question per interview: 100%
163	- Memory: second session opens with last session's weak spots: works on 3 of 3 tries
164	- Median turn latency: local ~4B vs hosted larger Gemma
165	- The friend's verdict, quoted
166	
167	## 9. Risks and mitigations
168	
169	| Risk | Mitigation |
170	|---|---|
171	| ~4B Gemma too weak for agent tool use | Keep tools few and simple; deterministic code does validation and scoring; compare with hosted larger Gemma and default hosted mode to it if needed |
172	| Mastra + small model structured output is flaky | zod repair path; Phase 0 spike before committing |
173	| Entire checkpoint format harder to parse than expected | Fall back to commit-level file lists from checkpoints; use Viva's own repo as the test fixture |
174	| Gemma on Render CPU too slow or too costly | Fallback to hosted Gemma endpoint, say so in the post |
175	| ElevenLabs STT timestamps missing or inconsistent | Compute pace and fillers from transcript only; pauses become optional |
176	| Scope too big for the weekend | Cut order in PHASES.md; never cut core interview, Mastra, or Entire provenance |
177	| Running out of time for the post | Post work starts Sunday night |
178	
179	## 10. Submission checklist (DEV)
180	
181	- [ ] Post created from the official Submission Template (tags: devchallenge, weekendchallenge, hf26challenge)
182	- [ ] Sections: What I Built, Demo, Code, How I Built It, Why Does Open Innovation Matter?, My Agent Session, Prize Categories
183	- [ ] Story: the friend, the freeze moment, the AI-coding angle
184	- [ ] Demo video (Wasih's demo skill) with ElevenLabs narration, Wi-Fi-off moment, memory moment, AI-written-code question, dogfood scene
185	- [ ] Partner sections: Gemma, Render, Mastra, Entire, ElevenLabs, Sentry, each with something specific
186	- [ ] "Why this code exists" section with 3 `entire explain` excerpts
187	- [ ] Agent session embedded via DevRelay (`agent_session` tag) or linked
188	- [ ] Prize Categories lists all six
189	- [ ] Friend's reaction quoted
190	- [ ] Repo public, README complete, Deploy to Render button works
191	- [ ] Rules re-checked: eligibility (18+, country), team handles if any

Check the current state: the model page capability badges, Ollama docs on tool calling (docs.ollama.com), and any newer Gemma variant (e.g. functiongemma, gemma3n, gemma 4) that does support tools. Research complete. Two findings change the likely design: Entire no longer stores checkpoints on a branch by default, and Mastra is now on AI SDK v7.

## Part A: Mastra

**1. Versions**
- `@mastra/core` is 1.74.0 and requires Node `>=22.13.0` (https://registry.npmjs.org/@mastra/core/latest).
- It bundles `@ai-sdk/provider` v5, v6 and v7 side by side; the Next.js guide uses `version: 'v7'`, and `ai` latest is 7.0.127 (https://mastra.ai/guides/getting-started/next-js).
- Zod peer range is `^3.25.0 || ^4.0.0`.

**2. Ollama / custom OpenAI-compatible URL**
- The built-in model router is the documented route for local models (https://mastra.ai/models):
  ```ts
  import { Agent } from "@mastra/core/agent";
  const agent = new Agent({
    id: "my-agent", name: "My Agent", instructions: "You are a helpful assistant",
    model: { id: "custom/my-qwen3-model", url: "http://your-custom-openai-compatible-endpoint.com/v1" }
  })
  ```
- Docs say `url` must be the base URL, not the chat endpoint, and that `provider/model` form sends a bare model name. `apiKey` and `headers` are also accepted on the object; `api: "responses"` is opt-in and Chat Completions is the default.
- So for Ollama it would be `{ id: "ollama/<gemma tag>", url: "http://localhost:11434/v1" }`. This is my inference: the docs only show LM Studio (`lmstudio/...`, `http://localhost:1234/v1`).
- Mastra's Ollama page instead says `pnpm add ollama-ai-provider-v2` and shows no code (https://mastra.ai/models/providers/ollama). That package is 4.0.1 with peers `ai ^7.0.0` and `zod ^4.0.16`.
- `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` is 3.0.62; I did not find a Mastra doc snippet using it.

**3. `createTool`** (https://mastra.ai/reference/tools/create-tool)
```ts
import { createTool } from '@mastra/core/tools'
createTool({ id, description, inputSchema: z.object({...}), outputSchema: z.object({...}),
  execute: async (input, context) => output })
```
- `input` is the validated input directly, not wrapped in `{ context }`.
- `context` carries `requestContext`, `abortSignal`, `agent`, `workflow`, `mcp`, `observe`.

**4. Structured output** (https://mastra.ai/docs/agents/structured-output)
- `const res = await agent.generate(prompt, { structuredOutput: { schema } })`, then read `res.object`.
- `jsonPromptInjection`: `false` (native), `'inline'`, `true`/`'system'`, or `'auto'` (prompt injection for models without native support).
- `model`: a separate structuring model.
- `errorStrategy`: `'strict'` (default, throws), `'warn'`, or `'fallback'` with `fallbackValue`.
- `instructions`: a compact description injected instead of the schema.

**5. Memory**
- Install `@mastra/memory` (1.35.0) and `@mastra/libsql` (1.25.0) (https://mastra.ai/docs/memory/overview).
- Storage: `new LibSQLStore({ id: 'mastra-storage', url: 'file:./storage.db' })` (https://mastra.ai/reference/storage/libsql).
- Per call: `agent.generate(msg, { memory: { resource: 'user-123', thread: 'conversation-123' } })`.
- Working memory: `new Memory({ storage, options: { workingMemory: { enabled: true, scope: 'resource', template } } })`, with `template` or `schema` but not both (https://mastra.ai/docs/memory/working-memory).
- File storage does not work on serverless platforms with ephemeral filesystems.
- Relative `file:` paths have a reported Next.js path issue (https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/issues/4507); I saw only the title, so use an absolute path to be safe.
- Missing `@libsql/win32-x64-msvc` binary errors on Windows are reported in other libsql projects, not Mastra specifically (https://github.com/tursodatabase/libsql/issues/1797, https://github.com/payloadcms/payload/issues/9860).

**6. Adding to Next.js**
- The guide uses `pnpm dlx mastra@latest init`, which creates `src/mastra/index.ts`, `agents/` and `tools/`.
- Then `pnpm add @mastra/ai-sdk@latest @ai-sdk/react ai`; the route handler uses `handleChatStream({ mastra, agentId, version: 'v7', params })`.
- Optional: `@mastra/next` plus `hono` to mount Mastra's full HTTP API.
- `serverExternalPackages: ['@mastra/*']` in `next.config.ts` is documented for Vercel deployment (https://mastra.ai/docs/deployment/web-framework). The getting-started guide does not mention it.

**7. Sentry**
- Official exporter `@mastra/sentry` 1.2.23, with `@mastra/observability` (https://mastra.ai/docs/observability/tracing/exporters/sentry):
  ```ts
  observability: new Observability({ configs: { sentry: { serviceName: 'my-service',
    exporters: [ new SentryExporter({ dsn: process.env.SENTRY_DSN!, environment: 'production', tracesSampleRate: 1.0 }) ] } } })
  ```
- Sentry's own `Sentry.vercelAIIntegration({ recordInputs, recordOutputs })` is on by default when tracing is configured, Node runtime only (not Edge), and supports `ai` `>=3.0.0 <=7` (https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/guides/nextjs/configuration/integrations/vercelai/).
- Do not combine it with AI SDK v7's `registerTelemetry`, which duplicates spans.

## Part B: Entire

Sources: https://github.com/entireio/cli README and `docs/architecture/` (`sessions-and-checkpoints.md`, `ref-checkpoint-backend.md`, `attribution.md`, `claude-hooks-integration.md`), plus https://docs.entire.io. Latest release is v0.11.3 (2026-09-25).

**1. Windows install (native)**
- `irm https://entire.io/install.ps1 | iex` (PowerShell 5.1+; uses Scoop when available).
- Or `scoop bucket add entire https://github.com/entireio/scoop-bucket.git` then `scoop install entire/entire`.
- Or `go install github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire@latest`.
- No winget or npm route is listed.

**2. Setup**
- `entire enable --agent claude-code`, or `entire agent add claude-code` on a repo that is already enabled.
- Useful flags: `--force`, `--local`, `--skip-push-sessions`, `--checkpoint-remote github:org/repo`, `--checkpoint-push-remote <name>`, `--absolute-git-hook-path`.
- There is only one strategy, manual-commit: "Entire never creates commits on the active branch". Auto-commit is not mentioned.
- Git hooks: `prepare-commit-msg` (adds the trailer), `post-commit` (condenses the checkpoint), `post-rewrite`, `pre-push`.
- Claude Code hooks go in `.claude/settings.json`: `SessionStart`, `UserPromptSubmit`, `Stop`, `PreToolUse[Agent]`, `PostToolUse[Agent]`, `PostToolUse[TaskCreate|TaskUpdate]`, each running `entire hooks claude-code …`.
- "Always link" is `commit_linking: "always"` (default `prompt`, which asks "Link this commit to session context? [Y]es / [n]o / [a]lways") (https://docs.entire.io/guides/checkpoints/capture-checkpoints.md).

**3. Storage format**
- The default is now one ref per checkpoint: `refs/entire/checkpoints/<shard>/<id>`, where "`<shard>` is the last two characters of the ID". Settings record it as `"checkpoints": {"primary": {"type": "git-refs"}}`.
- IDs are 26-character ULIDs; older checkpoints have 12-character hex IDs.
- The legacy backend is the branch `entire/checkpoints/v1`, sharded `<id[:2]>/<id[2:]>/`. A repo can hold both formats.
- The ref's commit tree root is the checkpoint itself:
  ```
  metadata.json
  0/metadata.json  0/full.jsonl  0/transcript.jsonl  0/prompt.txt  0/content_hash.txt
  1/...            tasks/<tool-use-id>/{agent-<id>.jsonl, task.json}
  ```
- There is no `context.md` in the current layout.
- Root `metadata.json` has `cli_version`, `checkpoint_id`, `strategy`, `branch`, `checkpoints_count`, `files_touched`, `sessions[]` and `token_usage`.
- Temporary shadow branches are named `entire/<commit[:7]>-<worktreeHash[:6]>` and are never pushed.
- Commit trailers: `Entire-Checkpoint: <id>` and `Entire-Attribution: 73% agent (146/200 lines)`.
- Attribution fields: `agent_lines`, `human_added`, `human_modified`, `human_removed`, `total_committed`, `total_lines_changed`, `agent_percentage`.

**4. Commands**
- Exist today: `entire status` (`--json`), `entire doctor` (`trace`, `logs`, `bundle`, `migrate-checkpoints`), `entire checkpoint list|explain|tokens|search`, `entire session list|info|current|stop|attach|adopt|resume|tokens`, `entire search`, `entire clean`, `entire configure`, `entire agent`.
- `entire checkpoint explain <id|commit-ref>` takes `--checkpoint`, `--commit`, `--session`, `--full`, `--raw-transcript`, `--short`, `--generate`, `--json` (https://docs.entire.io/cli-reference/checkpoint.md).
- Top-level `entire explain` and `entire rewind` appear in neither the README nor the CLI reference; `entire session resume <branch>` is the closest to rewind.
- `entire blame` and `entire why` are experimental.

**5. Push and GitHub API**
- Yes: `strategy_options.push_sessions` defaults to `true`, and the pre-push hook pushes queued checkpoint refs to one elected remote (usually `origin`), fast-forward only.
- They are not a branch, so they will not appear in the branches API or UI.
- They are readable over REST. I confirmed on the public `entireio/cli` repo that `GET /repos/entireio/cli/git/matching-refs/entire/checkpoints` returns 200 with refs.
- `GET /git/trees/<commit sha>?recursive=1` on one of them returned the layout above; `full.jsonl` there was about 3 MB, so use the blobs API rather than contents.
- `git ls-remote` showed 59 such refs.

**6. Redaction**
- Secrets are redacted automatically before a checkpoint is written, using the Betterleaks scanner, and replaced with `REDACTED` (https://docs.entire.io/guides/configuration/privacy-and-redaction.md).
- PII redaction is opt-in (`redaction.pii.*`, replaced with e.g. `[REDACTED_EMAIL]`).
- It is "best-effort", images are not scanned, and "If your repository is public, so are they" (https://docs.entire.io/security.md).

## DevRelay

- It exists: "an MCP server and skill pack" connecting coding agents to DEV and MLH (https://devrelay.com/).
- Install on macOS/Linux with `curl -fsSL https://devrelay.com/install.sh | sh`. The script itself points Windows users to `iwr -useb https://devrelay.com/install.ps1 | iex`.
- For Claude Code it writes a `devrelay-gateway` MCP entry (binary `dev_mlh_mcp_server --stdio`) into `~/.claude.json` and syncs skills; restart the agent afterwards.
- The site says "Save an agent transcript to DEV and embed it in a post". DEV's own post describes manual upload at https://dev.to/agent_sessions/new (https://dev.to/devteam/share-embed-and-curate-agent-sessions-on-dev-beta-5bj6).

## Could not verify

- The exact Ollama `id` prefix for the Mastra router, and whether Gemma tool calling or structured output works through it.
- A Mastra-specific libsql failure on Windows; the content and status of issue #4507.
- Whether `serverExternalPackages` is needed for local `next dev` or `next build`.
- Whether `mastra init` is strictly required; docs show no manual-install path for Next.js.
- `experimental_telemetry` wording in the Sentry docs (not returned by the page fetch).
- `entire rewind`: no doc states it was removed, it is just absent. `KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.md` has no Windows entries.
- The contents of DevRelay's `install.ps1`, and the name of its session-upload tool or skill (it is not in the tool list on the homepage).
- The `{% agent_session ID %}` embed syntax: it came from a search summary only, not from a page I read.</result>

# Viva: Phase 0 plan (setup, research, spikes)

## Context

Viva is a weekend-challenge build (deadline Mon 5 Oct 2026, 12:29 PM IST). Phase 0 has a 3 h timebox and exists to remove the risks that could sink the architecture before real coding starts: can a ~4B Gemma on a 16 GB laptop do tool calls and structured output through Mastra, what do Entire checkpoints actually look like, and which hosted Gemma do we compare against. No code has been written; the repo has only `CLAUDE.md`, `PRD.md`, `PHASES.md` (untracked, at the root) and no commits.

## 1. What I understood (5 bullets)

- **Viva** reads a student's project (GitHub URL or local folder), builds a `ProjectBrief`, and runs a mock viva with follow-ups grounded in the student's actual answers, ending in a scored report.
- **Standout feature:** it reads Entire checkpoints to learn which code an AI agent wrote and from which prompt, and asks about exactly that code.
- **Gemma is the brain** (local on Ollama, a larger Gemma hosted for the Render demo and comparison); **Mastra** runs the agent with tools (`readFile`, `getProvenance`) and cross-session memory of weak spots. Deterministic work (path validation, scoring, state machine) stays in plain typed functions.
- **Supporting layers:** ElevenLabs (voice + delivery metrics), Sentry (agent traces with quality attributes), Render (one-click blueprint). Wasih must be able to explain every line and writes the post himself.
- **Phase 0** = scaffold the repo, turn on session capture (Entire, DevRelay), pick the models, run two spikes (Mastra + small Gemma, Entire format), read partner docs, benchmark local vs hosted, and collect fixtures. Its output is decisions in `docs/DECISIONS.md`, not features.

## 2. Research findings (checked today; items marked ⚠ need confirming when we run them)

### Local machine (measured)
- Node **22.11.0**, pnpm 10.33.4, Ollama 0.35.1 (no models pulled), Entire CLI 0.11.3 (not enabled here), Docker, Go, `gh` logged in as AbdulWasih05.
- 15.9 GB RAM, NVIDIA MX130 (small VRAM, so mostly CPU inference).
- Remote `AbdulWasih05/Viva` exists, public, empty, created 2026-10-03 (inside the window). Local branch is `master`; CLAUDE context says main branch is `main`.

### Gemma
- **Gemma 4 is current** (E2B, E4B = 4.5B effective, 12B, 26B, 31B; Apache 2.0; native system role and function calling).
- Ollama tag **`gemma4:e4b`**: badges vision, **tools**, thinking, audio; Q4_K_M; 128K context. ⚠ Download size was reported as 6.6 GB by one page and 9.5 GB by another; confirm at pull time.
- Fallback tags: `gemma4:e2b` (~4.6 GB), then `gemma3:4b` (3.3 GB, **no tools badge**, would need tools driven by deterministic code).
- Ollama defaults to a **4k context** on this machine; raise with `OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH` (the `/v1` endpoint cannot set `num_ctx` per request). `tool_choice` is not supported on Ollama's `/v1`.
- Images are accepted by all Gemma 4 sizes, so Phase 8 is possible.

### Hosted larger Gemma
- **Google AI Studio / Gemini API:** `gemma-4-31b-it` and `gemma-4-26b-a4b-it`, free, system instructions + function calling supported. ⚠ Rate limits unpublished; JSON mode for Gemma and Gemma via the OpenAI-compatible base URL (`https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai/`) not confirmed in docs.
- **OpenRouter:** `google/gemma-4-31b-it:free`, tools + `response_format` listed; 20 RPM, 50 req/day (1000/day after buying $10 credit).
- **DeepInfra:** `google/gemma-4-31B-it`, $0.15 / $0.40 per 1M tokens (paid fallback).

### Mastra
- `@mastra/core` 1.74.0, **requires Node >= 22.13.0** (we have 22.11.0, must upgrade). Uses AI SDK v7; zod 3.25+ or 4.
- Custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint via the built-in model router: `model: { id: "<provider>/<model>", url: "<base url>/v1", apiKey? }`. ⚠ Docs show LM Studio only; the Ollama form is inferred. Fallback: `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` (`createOpenAICompatible`).
- `createTool({ id, description, inputSchema, outputSchema, execute: async (input, context) => ... })`.
- Structured output: `agent.generate(prompt, { structuredOutput: { schema, jsonPromptInjection, errorStrategy, fallbackValue } })`, read `res.object`.
- Memory: `@mastra/memory` + `@mastra/libsql`, `new LibSQLStore({ id, url: "file:..." })`, per call `memory: { resource, thread }`. Use an absolute file path (a relative-path issue under Next.js is reported).
- Sentry: official `@mastra/sentry` exporter exists (with `@mastra/observability`).

### Entire (differs from what PHASES.md assumed in places)
- Default backend is **one git ref per checkpoint**: `refs/entire/checkpoints/<shard>/<id>` (not a branch). Tree: `metadata.json`, `0/prompt.txt`, `0/full.jsonl`, `0/transcript.jsonl`, `0/metadata.json`.
- Root `metadata.json` has `files_touched`, `sessions[]`, `token_usage`. Commits get trailers `Entire-Checkpoint: <id>` and `Entire-Attribution: 73% agent (146/200 lines)`. So file-level provenance is available; attribution is per commit, ⚠ per-line data not confirmed.
- Refs are pushed on `git push` by default and are **readable via GitHub REST** (`git/matching-refs/entire/checkpoints`, then trees and blobs) on public repos; verified by the research agent on `entireio/cli`.
- The command is **`entire checkpoint explain <id|sha>`**; a top-level `entire explain` is not in the CLI help. Docs wording gets corrected in DECISIONS.md.
- Secrets are redacted best-effort before a checkpoint is written; transcripts on a public repo are public.

### Render / ElevenLabs / Sentry (read only, used in Phases 5 to 7)
- **Render:** private services and disks are **paid only**. An 8 GB instance (`4c-8g`) is roughly $175/mo by third-party pricing, about $17 for 3 days ⚠ (official price page did not load). Free web service spins down after 15 min. Deploy button: `https://render.com/deploy?repo=<repo url>`. No official Ollama template found.
- **ElevenLabs:** SDK `@elevenlabs/elevenlabs-js`; TTS model `eleven_flash_v2_5`; STT `POST /v1/speech-to-text` with `scribe_v2`, `words[]` with `text/start/end/type`. Filler words are kept unless `no_verbatim` is set (good for delivery coaching). Free tier 10k credits/month ⚠ STT burns about 330 credits/min by an unconfirmed snippet. Voice IDs to be picked via `GET /v2/voices`.
- **Sentry:** `npx @sentry/wizard@latest -i nextjs`; `vercelAIIntegration` is on by default (set `recordInputs/recordOutputs: false` for privacy); manual spans `gen_ai.invoke_agent` / `gen_ai.chat` / `gen_ai.execute_tool` with `span.setAttribute`. Free plan: 5M spans, 10 dashboards.

## 3. Plan for tasks 0.1 to 0.8

Order is changed slightly: Entire is enabled **before** the first commit so the scaffold commit is already linked.

### 0.1 Repo and tooling
1. **Upgrade Node** to >= 22.13 (Wasih runs it, installer needs admin): `winget install OpenJS.NodeJS.LTS` or nvm-windows. Verify `node --version`.
2. `git branch -M main` (remote already set to `AbdulWasih05/Viva`).
3. Scaffold in the scratchpad, then copy in (the folder name `Personal-viva` has a capital letter and existing files, both of which `create-next-app` rejects):
   `pnpm create next-app@latest viva --ts --tailwind --eslint --app --src-dir --import-alias "@/*" --use-pnpm` (confirm flags with `--help` first), copy everything except `.git` into the repo, set `"name": "viva"`.
4. `pnpm add zod` and `pnpm add -D vitest tsx`.
5. `package.json` scripts: `typecheck: tsc --noEmit`, `test: vitest run`, `eval: tsx scripts/eval.ts`, `bench: tsx scripts/bench-models.ts`. One trivial Vitest test so `pnpm test` is meaningful.
6. Move `PRD.md` and `PHASES.md` into `docs/` (CLAUDE.md already points there). Create `docs/PROGRESS.md`, `docs/DECISIONS.md`, `docs/post/.gitkeep`, `.env.example` (variables from CLAUDE.md), and add `.env`, `.viva/`, `.mastra/` to `.gitignore`. Fill the Commands section of `CLAUDE.md`.
7. Verify: `pnpm dev` (page loads), `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm test`. Commit `chore: scaffold Next.js app with tooling`, `git push -u origin main`.

### 0.2 Session capture (20 min timebox)
- `entire enable --agent claude-code`, then set commit linking to "always" (via `entire configure`; check `entire configure --help` for the exact flag). This writes hooks into `.claude/settings.json`, so **the Claude Code session likely needs a restart** to pick them up.
- Verify after the scaffold commit: `entire status`, `entire checkpoint list`, `git for-each-ref refs/entire/checkpoints/`.
- DevRelay: Wasih runs `iwr -useb https://devrelay.com/install.ps1 | iex` himself (remote script that edits `~/.claude.json`; needs his DEV account), then restarts Claude Code.
- Write the privacy rule into DECISIONS.md: public repo means public transcripts; keys only in `.env`.

### 0.3 Gemma choice
- `ollama pull gemma4:e4b`, `ollama show gemma4:e4b` (confirm `tools` capability and real size).
- Set `OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=8192` as a user env var and restart Ollama; `ollama ps` during a run to record RAM use and CPU/GPU split.
- One timed prompt for tokens/sec. If it swaps or is unusably slow: `ollama pull gemma4:e2b` and repeat.
- Hosted: create a Google AI Studio key, one `curl` to the OpenAI-compatible endpoint with `gemma-4-31b-it`. If Gemma is not served there, switch to OpenRouter `google/gemma-4-31b-it:free`.
- Record: chosen tags, sizes, context, limits, image support.

### 0.4 Mastra spike (45 min, decides architecture)
- `pnpm add @mastra/core @mastra/memory @mastra/libsql` (add `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` only if the model router form fails).
- One throwaway file `scripts/spikes/mastra.ts`, run with `pnpm tsx`, with four checks printed as pass/fail:
  1. plain `agent.generate` against Ollama via `{ id, url: OLLAMA_BASE_URL }`
  2. a `readFile` stub tool gets called, 5 runs, count successes
  3. `structuredOutput` with a small zod schema, 5 runs, count valid; retry with `jsonPromptInjection` if native fails
  4. memory with `LibSQLStore` at an absolute `.viva/memory.db` path survives two separate process runs
- Decision rule: if tool calls succeed in fewer than 4 of 5 runs on the local model, tools are called by deterministic code between agent steps in local mode, and the agent uses native tool calls only on the hosted model. Log numbers `[POST]`.

### 0.5 Entire format spike (30 min)
- `git for-each-ref refs/entire/checkpoints/`, `git ls-tree -r <ref>`, `git show <ref>:metadata.json`, `git show <ref>:0/prompt.txt`, `git log -1 --format=%B` (trailers), `entire checkpoint explain <id> --json`.
- After push: `gh api repos/AbdulWasih05/Viva/git/matching-refs/entire/checkpoints`, then one tree and one blob call.
- Document in DECISIONS.md where the prompt, transcript, changed files and attribution live, and whether line-level data exists (decides cut-order item 7).

### 0.6 Partner research
- Already done above; copy the findings and source links into DECISIONS.md. Wasih claims credits at hacktoberfest.com/my/promos (login required).

### 0.7 Model benchmark
- `scripts/bench-models.ts` using the same provider config as the spike: one brief prompt + one question prompt on a small fixture, 10 runs each on local and hosted.
- Records structured-output validity, median latency, and whether the question names a real file. Results into PROGRESS.md tagged `[POST]`; set `OLLAMA_MODEL` and `HOSTED_MODEL`.
- If a free tier limit (for example OpenRouter 50/day) blocks 10 runs, reduce runs and say so; no invented numbers.

### 0.8 Fixtures
- Pick 3 small public repos (Node API, React app, Python app), one of them Wasih's if he has a public one; snapshot only the files the ingest heuristic would select into `fixtures/<name>/` with a `SOURCE.md` (URL, commit SHA, licence).
- Note the 4th fixture (this repo with its checkpoints) for Phase 3.

### Close out
- Tick boxes in `docs/PHASES.md`, append to `docs/PROGRESS.md` (what changed, how verified, `[POST]` lines, a short "How it works"), commit per subtask.

## Accounts, keys and money

| Item | Needed for | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| Node upgrade to >= 22.13 | Mastra | free, admin install |
| Google AI Studio API key | hosted Gemma (0.3, 0.7) | free |
| OpenRouter account (fallback) | hosted Gemma | free at 50 req/day; $10 lifts to 1000/day |
| DEV account + DevRelay install | agent session embed | free |
| Entire login | only if local checkpoints need it (expected not) | free |
| hacktoberfest.com promos | Render and ElevenLabs credits | free, login |
| Render paid instance + disk | Phase 5 private Ollama | about $17 for 3 days unless credits cover it (unverified price) |
| ElevenLabs key | Phase 6 | free tier may be tight for STT |
| Sentry account + DSN | Phase 7 | free |

Nothing in Phase 0 costs money.

## 4. Open questions for Wasih

1. **Prize categories:** the DEV challenge page fetch showed Render, TabPFN, Tinker and Qualcomm as $200 categories and was cut off before the rest. Can you confirm on the page that Gemma, Mastra, Entire, ElevenLabs and Sentry are real categories? It affects what we protect in the cut order.
2. **Node upgrade:** OK to upgrade Node to the current 22 LTS (or 24) before we start? Mastra will not install cleanly otherwise.
3. **Hosted Gemma:** Google AI Studio first, OpenRouter as fallback. Fine, and can you create the key and put it in `.env` yourself?
4. **Local model:** try `gemma4:e4b` first and drop to `gemma4:e2b` if the laptop struggles. Agreed? (CLAUDE.md says "about 4B"; E4B is 4.5B effective.)
5. **Render spend:** if partner credits do not cover an 8 GB private service, do we go straight to cut-order item 3 (hosted Gemma behind the Render web service)?
6. **Fixtures:** do you have a public repo of your own to use, and is the friend's project public (it is the Phase 9 test)?
7. **Branch and docs:** rename `master` to `main` and move `PRD.md` / `PHASES.md` into `docs/`. Any objection?
8. **DevRelay and Entire login:** will you run the DevRelay installer yourself, and are you already logged in to Entire?

## Verification (end of Phase 0)

- `pnpm dev`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm test` all pass.
- `entire checkpoint list` shows a checkpoint for at least one commit, and the same ref is returned by the GitHub API.
- The Mastra spike prints pass/fail counts for all four checks on the local model.
- `pnpm bench` prints validity, median latency and real-file rate for both models.
- `docs/DECISIONS.md` records: model tags, provider wiring, tool-calling decision, Entire format, hosted limits. `docs/PHASES.md` Phase 0 boxes ticked.

Revision 2 applies Wasih's review: hosted Gemma becomes the main model, the benchmark and fixtures shrink, Render cut item 3 is applied now, and the Next.js + LibSQL bundling risk is tested through a real API route.

## Decisions locked in this revision (all go to `docs/DECISIONS.md`)

1. **Main model = hosted Gemma 4 31B** (`gemma-4-31b-it` on Google AI Studio) for development, evals and the demo. Reason: the MX130 has about 2 GB of video memory, so `gemma4:e4b` runs mostly on CPU and one interview turn could take 1 to 3 minutes. OpenRouter `google/gemma-4-31b-it:free` is the fallback.
2. **Local Gemma (`gemma4:e4b`) is used only for** the Wi-Fi-off privacy clip and a small benchmark. Drop to `gemma4:e2b` only if e4b cannot produce the clip. `LLM_PROVIDER` default becomes `hosted`; local mode still works by switching the env var.

If partner credits cover it, use a paid Starter instance so a judge does not hit the free tier's cold start (free web services sleep after 15 minutes idle).
4. **Benchmark:** 3 local runs and 5 hosted runs per prompt; the rest of the measuring folds into Phase 1 evals.
5. **Fixtures:** 2 public repos plus Viva itself.
6. **Structured output fallback on Ollama:** if `/v1` JSON output is flaky, call Ollama's native API with a JSON schema in the `format` field, not prompt tricks.
7. **Prize categories confirmed by Wasih** from the challenge page: Gemma ($200), Render ($200), Mastra, Entire, ElevenLabs, Sentry Agent Tracing ($100 each). The cut order's "never cut" list stands.

# Viva: Phase 0 plan (setup, research, spikes)

## Context

Viva is a weekend-challenge build (deadline Mon 5 Oct 2026, 12:29 PM IST). Phase 0 has a 3 h timebox and exists to remove the risks that could sink the architecture before real coding starts: can a ~4B Gemma on a 16 GB laptop do tool calls and structured output through Mastra, what do Entire checkpoints actually look like, and which hosted Gemma do we compare against. No code has been written; the repo has only `CLAUDE.md`, `PRD.md`, `PHASES.md` (untracked, at the root) and no commits.

## 1. What I understood (5 bullets)

- **Viva** reads a student's project (GitHub URL or local folder), builds a `ProjectBrief`, and runs a mock viva with follow-ups grounded in the student's actual answers, ending in a scored report.
- **Standout feature:** it reads Entire checkpoints to learn which code an AI agent wrote and from which prompt, and asks about exactly that code.
- **Gemma is the brain** (local on Ollama, a larger Gemma hosted for the Render demo and comparison); **Mastra** runs the agent with tools (`readFile`, `getProvenance`) and cross-session memory of weak spots. Deterministic work (path validation, scoring, state machine) stays in plain typed functions.
- **Supporting layers:** ElevenLabs (voice + delivery metrics), Sentry (agent traces with quality attributes), Render (one-click blueprint). Wasih must be able to explain every line and writes the post himself.
- **Phase 0** = scaffold the repo, turn on session capture (Entire, DevRelay), pick the models, run two spikes (Mastra + small Gemma, Entire format), read partner docs, benchmark local vs hosted, and collect fixtures. Its output is decisions in `docs/DECISIONS.md`, not features.

## 2. Research findings (checked today; items marked ⚠ need confirming when we run them)

### Local machine (measured)
- Node **22.11.0**, pnpm 10.33.4, Ollama 0.35.1 (no models pulled), Entire CLI 0.11.3 (not enabled here), Docker, Go, `gh` logged in as AbdulWasih05.
- 15.9 GB RAM, NVIDIA MX130 (small VRAM, so mostly CPU inference).
- Remote `AbdulWasih05/Viva` exists, public, empty, created 2026-10-03 (inside the window). Local branch is `master`; CLAUDE context says main branch is `main`.

### Gemma
- **Gemma 4 is current** (E2B, E4B = 4.5B effective, 12B, 26B, 31B; Apache 2.0; native system role and function calling).
- Ollama tag **`gemma4:e4b`**: badges vision, **tools**, thinking, audio; Q4_K_M; 128K context. ⚠ Download size was reported as 6.6 GB by one page and 9.5 GB by another; confirm at pull time.
- Fallback tags: `gemma4:e2b` (~4.6 GB), then `gemma3:4b` (3.3 GB, **no tools badge**, would need tools driven by deterministic code).
- Ollama defaults to a **4k context** on this machine; raise with `OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH` (the `/v1` endpoint cannot set `num_ctx` per request). `tool_choice` is not supported on Ollama's `/v1`.
- Images are accepted by all Gemma 4 sizes, so Phase 8 is possible.

### Hosted larger Gemma
- **Google AI Studio / Gemini API:** `gemma-4-31b-it` and `gemma-4-26b-a4b-it`, free, system instructions + function calling supported. ⚠ Rate limits unpublished; JSON mode for Gemma and Gemma via the OpenAI-compatible base URL (`https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai/`) not confirmed in docs.
- **OpenRouter:** `google/gemma-4-31b-it:free`, tools + `response_format` listed; 20 RPM, 50 req/day (1000/day after buying $10 credit).
- **DeepInfra:** `google/gemma-4-31B-it`, $0.15 / $0.40 per 1M tokens (paid fallback).

### Mastra
- `@mastra/core` 1.74.0, **requires Node >= 22.13.0** (we have 22.11.0, must upgrade). Uses AI SDK v7; zod 3.25+ or 4.
- Custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint via the built-in model router: `model: { id: "<provider>/<model>", url: "<base url>/v1", apiKey? }`. ⚠ Docs show LM Studio only; the Ollama form is inferred. Fallback: `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` (`createOpenAICompatible`).
- `createTool({ id, description, inputSchema, outputSchema, execute: async (input, context) => ... })`.
- Structured output: `agent.generate(prompt, { structuredOutput: { schema, jsonPromptInjection, errorStrategy, fallbackValue } })`, read `res.object`.
- Memory: `@mastra/memory` + `@mastra/libsql`, `new LibSQLStore({ id, url: "file:..." })`, per call `memory: { resource, thread }`. Use an absolute file path (a relative-path issue under Next.js is reported).
- Sentry: official `@mastra/sentry` exporter exists (with `@mastra/observability`).

### Entire (differs from what PHASES.md assumed in places)
- Default backend is **one git ref per checkpoint**: `refs/entire/checkpoints/<shard>/<id>` (not a branch). Tree: `metadata.json`, `0/prompt.txt`, `0/full.jsonl`, `0/transcript.jsonl`, `0/metadata.json`.
- Root `metadata.json` has `files_touched`, `sessions[]`, `token_usage`. Commits get trailers `Entire-Checkpoint: <id>` and `Entire-Attribution: 73% agent (146/200 lines)`. So file-level provenance is available; attribution is per commit, ⚠ per-line data not confirmed.
- Refs are pushed on `git push` by default and are **readable via GitHub REST** (`git/matching-refs/entire/checkpoints`, then trees and blobs) on public repos; verified by the research agent on `entireio/cli`.
- The command is **`entire checkpoint explain <id|sha>`**; a top-level `entire explain` is not in the CLI help. Docs wording gets corrected in DECISIONS.md.
- Secrets are redacted best-effort before a checkpoint is written; transcripts on a public repo are public.

### Render / ElevenLabs / Sentry (read only, used in Phases 5 to 7)
- **Render:** private services and disks are **paid only**. An 8 GB instance (`4c-8g`) is roughly $175/mo by third-party pricing, about $17 for 3 days ⚠ (official price page did not load). Free web service spins down after 15 min. Deploy button: `https://render.com/deploy?repo=<repo url>`. No official Ollama template found.
- **ElevenLabs:** SDK `@elevenlabs/elevenlabs-js`; TTS model `eleven_flash_v2_5`; STT `POST /v1/speech-to-text` with `scribe_v2`, `words[]` with `text/start/end/type`. Filler words are kept unless `no_verbatim` is set (good for delivery coaching). Free tier 10k credits/month ⚠ STT burns about 330 credits/min by an unconfirmed snippet. Voice IDs to be picked via `GET /v2/voices`.
- **Sentry:** `npx @sentry/wizard@latest -i nextjs`; `vercelAIIntegration` is on by default (set `recordInputs/recordOutputs: false` for privacy); manual spans `gen_ai.invoke_agent` / `gen_ai.chat` / `gen_ai.execute_tool` with `span.setAttribute`. Free plan: 5M spans, 10 dashboards.

## 3. Plan for tasks 0.1 to 0.8

Order is changed slightly: Entire is enabled **before** the first commit so the scaffold commit is already linked.

### 0.1 Repo and tooling
1. **Upgrade Node** to >= 22.13 (Wasih runs it, installer needs admin): `winget install OpenJS.NodeJS.LTS` or nvm-windows. Verify `node --version`.
2. `git branch -M main` (remote already set to `AbdulWasih05/Viva`).
3. Scaffold in the scratchpad, then copy in (the folder name `Personal-viva` has a capital letter and existing files, both of which `create-next-app` rejects):
   `pnpm create next-app@latest viva --ts --tailwind --eslint --app --src-dir --import-alias "@/*" --use-pnpm` (confirm flags with `--help` first), copy everything except `.git` into the repo, set `"name": "viva"`.
4. `pnpm add zod` and `pnpm add -D vitest tsx`.
5. `package.json` scripts: `typecheck: tsc --noEmit`, `test: vitest run`, `eval: tsx scripts/eval.ts`, `bench: tsx scripts/bench-models.ts`. One trivial Vitest test so `pnpm test` is meaningful.
6. Move `PRD.md` and `PHASES.md` into `docs/` (CLAUDE.md already points there). Create `docs/PROGRESS.md`, `docs/DECISIONS.md`, `docs/post/.gitkeep`, `.env.example` (variables from CLAUDE.md), and add `.env`, `.viva/`, `.mastra/` to `.gitignore`. Fill the Commands section of `CLAUDE.md`.
7. Verify: `pnpm dev` (page loads), `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm test`. Commit `chore: scaffold Next.js app with tooling`, `git push -u origin main`.

### 0.2 Session capture (20 min timebox)
- `entire enable --agent claude-code`, then set commit linking to "always" (via `entire configure`; check `entire configure --help` for the exact flag). This writes hooks into `.claude/settings.json`, so **the Claude Code session likely needs a restart** to pick them up.
- Verify after the scaffold commit: `entire status`, `entire checkpoint list`, `git for-each-ref refs/entire/checkpoints/`.
- DevRelay: Wasih runs `iwr -useb https://devrelay.com/install.ps1 | iex` himself (remote script that edits `~/.claude.json`; needs his DEV account), then restarts Claude Code.
- Write the privacy rule into DECISIONS.md: public repo means public transcripts; keys only in `.env`.

### 0.3 Gemma choice
- `ollama pull gemma4:e4b`, `ollama show gemma4:e4b` (confirm `tools` capability and real size).
- Set `OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=8192` as a user env var and restart Ollama; `ollama ps` during a run to record RAM use and CPU/GPU split.
- One timed prompt for tokens/sec. If it swaps or is unusably slow: `ollama pull gemma4:e2b` and repeat.
- Hosted: create a Google AI Studio key, one `curl` to the OpenAI-compatible endpoint with `gemma-4-31b-it`. If Gemma is not served there, switch to OpenRouter `google/gemma-4-31b-it:free`.
- Record: chosen tags, sizes, context, limits, image support.

### 0.4 Mastra spike (45 min, decides architecture)
- `pnpm add @mastra/core @mastra/memory @mastra/libsql` (add `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` only if the model router form fails).
- One throwaway file `scripts/spikes/mastra.ts`, run with `pnpm tsx`, with four checks printed as pass/fail:
  1. plain `agent.generate` against Ollama via `{ id, url: OLLAMA_BASE_URL }`
  2. a `readFile` stub tool gets called, 5 runs, count successes
  3. `structuredOutput` with a small zod schema, 5 runs, count valid; retry with `jsonPromptInjection` if native fails
  4. memory with `LibSQLStore` at an absolute `.viva/memory.db` path survives two separate process runs
- Decision rule: if tool calls succeed in fewer than 4 of 5 runs on the local model, tools are called by deterministic code between agent steps in local mode, and the agent uses native tool calls only on the hosted model. Log numbers `[POST]`.

### 0.5 Entire format spike (30 min)
- `git for-each-ref refs/entire/checkpoints/`, `git ls-tree -r <ref>`, `git show <ref>:metadata.json`, `git show <ref>:0/prompt.txt`, `git log -1 --format=%B` (trailers), `entire checkpoint explain <id> --json`.
- After push: `gh api repos/AbdulWasih05/Viva/git/matching-refs/entire/checkpoints`, then one tree and one blob call.
- Document in DECISIONS.md where the prompt, transcript, changed files and attribution live, and whether line-level data exists (decides cut-order item 7).

### 0.6 Partner research
- Already done above; copy the findings and source links into DECISIONS.md. Wasih claims credits at hacktoberfest.com/my/promos (login required).

### 0.7 Model benchmark
- `scripts/bench-models.ts` using the same provider config as the spike: one brief prompt + one question prompt on a small fixture, 10 runs each on local and hosted.
- Records structured-output validity, median latency, and whether the question names a real file. Results into PROGRESS.md tagged `[POST]`; set `OLLAMA_MODEL` and `HOSTED_MODEL`.
- If a free tier limit (for example OpenRouter 50/day) blocks 10 runs, reduce runs and say so; no invented numbers.

### 0.8 Fixtures
- Pick 3 small public repos (Node API, React app, Python app), one of them Wasih's if he has a public one; snapshot only the files the ingest heuristic would select into `fixtures/<name>/` with a `SOURCE.md` (URL, commit SHA, licence).
- Note the 4th fixture (this repo with its checkpoints) for Phase 3.

### Close out
- Tick boxes in `docs/PHASES.md`, append to `docs/PROGRESS.md` (what changed, how verified, `[POST]` lines, a short "How it works"), commit per subtask.

## Accounts, keys and money

| Item | Needed for | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| Node upgrade to >= 22.13 | Mastra | free, admin install |
| Google AI Studio API key | hosted Gemma (0.3, 0.7) | free |
| OpenRouter account (fallback) | hosted Gemma | free at 50 req/day; $10 lifts to 1000/day |
| DEV account + DevRelay install | agent session embed | free |
| Entire login | only if local checkpoints need it (expected not) | free |
| hacktoberfest.com promos | Render and ElevenLabs credits | free, login |
| Render paid instance + disk | Phase 5 private Ollama | about $17 for 3 days unless credits cover it (unverified price) |
| ElevenLabs key | Phase 6 | free tier may be tight for STT |
| Sentry account + DSN | Phase 7 | free |

Nothing in Phase 0 costs money.

## 4. Open questions for Wasih

1. **Prize categories:** the DEV challenge page fetch showed Render, TabPFN, Tinker and Qualcomm as $200 categories and was cut off before the rest. Can you confirm on the page that Gemma, Mastra, Entire, ElevenLabs and Sentry are real categories? It affects what we protect in the cut order.
2. **Node upgrade:** OK to upgrade Node to the current 22 LTS (or 24) before we start? Mastra will not install cleanly otherwise.
3. **Hosted Gemma:** Google AI Studio first, OpenRouter as fallback. Fine, and can you create the key and put it in `.env` yourself?
4. **Local model:** try `gemma4:e4b` first and drop to `gemma4:e2b` if the laptop struggles. Agreed? (CLAUDE.md says "about 4B"; E4B is 4.5B effective.)
5. **Render spend:** if partner credits do not cover an 8 GB private service, do we go straight to cut-order item 3 (hosted Gemma behind the Render web service)?
6. **Fixtures:** do you have a public repo of your own to use, and is the friend's project public (it is the Phase 9 test)?
7. **Branch and docs:** rename `master` to `main` and move `PRD.md` / `PHASES.md` into `docs/`. Any objection?
8. **DevRelay and Entire login:** will you run the DevRelay installer yourself, and are you already logged in to Entire?

## Verification (end of Phase 0)

- `pnpm dev`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm test` all pass.
- `entire checkpoint list` shows a checkpoint for at least one commit, and the same ref is returned by the GitHub API.
- The Mastra spike prints pass/fail counts for all four checks on the local model.
- `pnpm bench` prints validity, median latency and real-file rate for both models.
- `docs/DECISIONS.md` records: model tags, provider wiring, tool-calling decision, Entire format, hosted limits. `docs/PHASES.md` Phase 0 boxes ticked.

input.content:
# Copy to .env and fill in. Never commit real keys (the repo and its Entire checkpoints are public).

# Which model the app talks to. "hosted" is the default for development and the demo;
# "ollama" is for offline / private use on your own machine.
LLM_PROVIDER=hosted

# Hosted Gemma (OpenAI-compatible endpoint). Default: Google AI Studio.
HOSTED_BASE_URL=https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai/
HOSTED_API_KEY=
HOSTED_MODEL=gemma-4-31b-it

# Local Gemma through Ollama's OpenAI-compatible endpoint.
OLLAMA_BASE_URL=http://localhost:11434/v1
OLLAMA_MODEL=gemma4:e4b

# Optional: raises the GitHub API rate limit when reading repos.
GITHUB_TOKEN=

# Voice (optional; text mode works without these).
ELEVENLABS_API_KEY=
ELEVENLABS_VOICE_FRIENDLY=
ELEVENLABS_VOICE_TOUGH=

# Tracing (optional).
SENTRY_DSN=

# true = local folders + memory are allowed. Must be false on Render.
LOCAL_MODE=true
MEMORY_DB_PATH=.viva/memory.db

# DECISIONS

Architecture choices and research surprises, newest at the bottom. One line of reason each. Items marked "unverified" are from docs or third parties and have not been run by us yet.

## Phase 0 (4 Oct 2026)

### Models

- **D1. Main model is hosted Gemma 4 31B** (`gemma-4-31b-it`, Google AI Studio, OpenAI-compatible endpoint) for development, evals and the demo. Reason: the laptop's MX130 has about 2 GB of video memory, so a local Gemma runs mostly on CPU and one interview turn could take 1 to 3 minutes. Fallback: OpenRouter `google/gemma-4-31b-it:free` (20 requests/min, 50 requests/day, 1000/day after buying $10 credit).
- **D2. Local Gemma is `gemma4:e4b` on Ollama**, used for the Wi-Fi-off privacy clip and a small benchmark only. Drop to `gemma4:e2b` only if e4b cannot produce the clip. `LLM_PROVIDER` defaults to `hosted`; switching the env var to `ollama` still runs everything locally.
- **D3. Gemma 4, not Gemma 3.** Gemma 4 is the current family and its Ollama page lists tool calling; `gemma3:4b` has no tools support on Ollama.
- **D4. Ollama context length.** Ollama defaults to a 4k context on machines with under 24 GB of video memory, and its OpenAI-compatible endpoint cannot set it per request. Set `OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH` (we start at 8192).
- **D5. Structured output fallback on Ollama.** If JSON through `/v1` is flaky, call Ollama's native API with a JSON schema in the `format` field. Reason: schema-constrained output beats prompt tricks.

### Hosting

- **D6. Render: no private Ollama service** (cut-order item 3 applied up front). The Render web service calls the hosted Gemma endpoint; `render.yaml` and the Deploy to Render button stay. Reason: private services and disks are paid only, and an 8 GB instance price could not be confirmed.
- **D7. Keeping the free Render service awake.** A `/api/health` route pinged every 5 minutes (UptimeRobot or a cron job) stops the 15-minute idle spin-down, so a judge does not wait for a cold start. One always-on service fits in the 750 free instance hours per month.

### Scope

- **D8. Benchmark size:** 3 local runs and 5 hosted runs per prompt; further measuring happens in Phase 1 evals. Reason: 10 CPU runs per prompt could take an hour.
- **D9. Fixtures:** 2 public repos plus Viva itself (was 3 plus Viva).
- **D10. Prize categories** confirmed by Wasih from the challenge page: Gemma ($200), Render ($200), Mastra, Entire, ElevenLabs, Sentry Agent Tracing ($100 each).
- **D11. ElevenLabs credits:** claim promo credits first; real voice only for testing and the video. Free tier is 10k credits/month; speech-to-text is reported at about 330 credits/min (unverified), so about 30 minutes.

### Tooling

- **D12. Node >= 22.13** is required by `@mastra/core` 1.74 (the laptop had 22.11.0).
- **D13. Scaffolded in a temp folder and copied in.** Reason: `create-next-app` rejects a folder name with capital letters (`Personal-viva`) and a non-empty folder.
- **D14. Next.js bundling and LibSQL.** `serverExternalPackages` lists `@libsql/client` and `@mastra/*` in `next.config.ts`, and memory is tested through a real API route in dev and in a production build. Reason: LibSQL is a native module and often breaks Next.js bundling.

### Entire

- **D15. Checkpoint storage** is one git ref per checkpoint, `refs/entire/checkpoints/<shard>/<id>` (`.entire/settings.json` shows `"type": "git-refs"`), not a branch. Format details to be confirmed on our own checkpoints in task 0.5.
- **D16. Command name:** it is `entire checkpoint explain <id|sha>`; there is no top-level `entire explain` in CLI 0.11.3.
- **D17. Privacy rule.** The repo is public and checkpoint refs are pushed with it, so session transcripts are public. Entire redacts detected secrets on a best-effort basis only. Keys live only in `.env` and are never pasted into a session.

### Research notes for later phases (unverified until used)

- **Mastra:** custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint via `model: { id, url, apiKey }` (docs show LM Studio only); fallback `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible`. Structured output via `agent.generate(prompt, { structuredOutput: { schema, jsonPromptInjection, errorStrategy, fallbackValue } })`. Memory via `@mastra/memory` + `@mastra/libsql`. Official Sentry exporter `@mastra/sentry`.
- **Entire over GitHub API:** `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/matching-refs/entire/checkpoints`, then trees and blobs (transcripts can be several MB, so use blobs, not contents).
- **ElevenLabs:** SDK `@elevenlabs/elevenlabs-js`; TTS model `eleven_flash_v2_5`; speech-to-text `POST /v1/speech-to-text` with `scribe_v2`, `words[]` of `{text, start, end, type}`; filler words are kept unless `no_verbatim` is set. Voice IDs from `GET /v2/voices`.
- **Sentry:** `npx @sentry/wizard@latest -i nextjs`; `vercelAIIntegration` is on by default, set `recordInputs` and `recordOutputs` to false; manual spans `gen_ai.invoke_agent`, `gen_ai.chat`, `gen_ai.execute_tool`. Free plan: 5M spans, 10 dashboards.
- **Render:** Deploy button URL `https://render.com/deploy?repo=<repo url>`; needs `render.yaml` at the repo root.

# PROGRESS

input.old_string: ### Research notes for later phases
input.new_string:
### Entire checkpoint format (task 0.5, verified on this repo's first checkpoint, CLI 0.11.3)

- **D18. Where things live.** Each checkpoint is a commit at `refs/entire/checkpoints/<last 2 chars of id>/<id>`. Its tree:
  - `metadata.json`: `checkpoint_id`, `branch`, `files_touched[]`, `sessions[]` (paths to the files below), `token_usage`
  - `0/metadata.json`: `session_id`, `agent`, `model`, `created_at`, `files_touched[]`, `initial_attribution`
  - `0/prompt.txt`: the prompt of the turn that led to the commit
  - `0/transcript.jsonl`: compact transcript, one JSON object per line with `type` (`user` / `assistant`), `ts`, `content[]`
  - `0/full.jsonl`: the raw agent transcript (1.3 MB for our first one)
- **D19. Link from code to checkpoint** is the commit trailer `Entire-Checkpoint: <id>` on the normal commit. Our commits did not get an `Entire-Attribution` trailer; attribution is only inside `0/metadata.json`.
- **D20. Provenance is file-level.** `initial_attribution` has counts only (`agent_lines`, `human_added`, `human_modified`, `total_committed`, `agent_percentage`), no line ranges. So the AI-authored map is: commit -> `files_touched` + agent percentage + prompt. Line-level provenance (cut-order item 7) is not available from the checkpoint and is dropped.
- **D21. `prompt.txt` is not always a human prompt.** `[WHY]` Our first checkpoint's `prompt.txt` held a background-task notification, because that was the latest turn before the commit. The provenance reader must skip prompts that start with `<task-notification>` or other system tags and fall back to the last real `user` line in `transcript.jsonl`.
- **D22. GitHub API access works on a public repo** (verified with `gh api`): `git/matching-refs/entire/checkpoints` lists the refs, `git/trees/<commit sha>?recursive=1` lists the files, `git/blobs/<sha>` returns base64 content, and the commit message from `commits/<sha>` carries the trailer. Hosted mode can use the same reader logic as local mode.
- **D23. PII redaction turned on.** The first pushed transcript contained an email address (from the session's own context) and local Windows paths. Secret redaction is on by default but PII redaction is not, so `.entire/settings.json` now sets `redaction.pii.enabled` and `email`. It only affects checkpoints written from now on.

### Research notes for later phases

No, Node is still 22.11.0, and I would not build on it.

- **Tests cannot run on it.** Vitest's bundler requires Node 22.12 or newer, so pnpm skipped its Windows binary and `pnpm test` fails at startup.
- **Mastra declares 22.13 or newer.** pnpm would probably still install it with a warning, but 22.12 is where Node began loading ES modules via `require()` by default, and packages that set this floor often depend on it. I have not tried Mastra on 22.11, so I can't say exactly where it would break.

Forcing the missing binary in by hand and ignoring the engine warnings might get past both, but any odd failure afterwards would be hard to tell apart from a real bug. The upgrade is a few minutes and stays within Node 22, so nothing else on your machine should change.

To upgrade:

1. Close Claude Code and anything else running Node (dev servers, other terminals). My earlier attempt failed with installer error 1603, most likely because Node was in use or the admin prompt was not accepted.
2. In a fresh PowerShell window, run `winget install --id OpenJS.NodeJS.22` and accept the admin prompt. Or download the 22.23.2 `.msi` from nodejs.org and run it.
3. Check `node --version` shows 22.23.2, then reopen Claude Code in this folder.

After that I'll run `pnpm install` again so the skipped binary gets picked up, and carry on with the Mastra spike once the AI Studio key is in `.env`.

questions.question: Hosted Gemma 4 31B is unreliable on AI Studio right now: it returned HTTP 500 on 6 of 10 calls (always with a system message on the OpenAI-compatible URL) and took 9 to 46 s when it worked. Gemma 4 26B on Google's native API with thinking set to minimal did system prompt, JSON schema and a tool call in 1.3 to 2.1 s each (3 of 3). Which hosted setup should be the main model?

options.label: 26B, native API (Recommended)
options.description: gemma-4-26b-a4b-it through the AI SDK's Google provider (@ai-sdk/google) with thinkingLevel minimal. Fast and everything worked. Changes decision D1: not 31B, and hosted no longer uses the OpenAI-compatible URL (Ollama still does).

options.label: 26B, OpenAI-compatible URL
options.description: Keeps one provider type for both modes. Works with a system message in about 8 to 10 s, but thinking cannot be turned off there and leaks into the answer as <thought> text that we would have to strip.

options.label: 31B via OpenRouter
options.description: Keeps 31B and the OpenAI-compatible stack. Untested, needs you to add an OpenRouter key, and the free tier is 50 requests/day (1000/day after $10 credit).

options.label: 26B main, 31B in benchmark only
options.description: Same as the recommended option, plus 31B is included in the Phase 0 benchmark as a third column so the post can show why it was not used.

questions.question: Your .env has only GEMINI_API_KEY, while .env.example and the docs use HOSTED_API_KEY. Which name should the code read?

options.label: Use GEMINI_API_KEY
options.description: I rename the variable in .env.example, CLAUDE.md and the code to GEMINI_API_KEY. You change nothing. HOSTED_BASE_URL / HOSTED_MODEL stay for the OpenRouter fallback.

options.label: Keep HOSTED_API_KEY
options.description: Docs stay as they are; you rename the variable in your .env yourself.

questions.question: Three commits already on origin/main carry a Co-Authored-By trailer, and one pushed Entire checkpoint transcript contains your Gmail address. What should I do about them?

options.label: Leave both as they are
options.description: No history rewrite. Only new commits and PRs are trailer-free, and email redaction applies to new checkpoints.

options.label: Rewrite main, delete the ref
options.description: I rewrite the three commits without trailers and force-push main, and delete the one checkpoint ref from GitHub. Force-push is safe here since nobody else has cloned, but it is a history rewrite.

options.label: Delete the ref only
options.description: Remove the checkpoint ref with the email from GitHub; leave the three commits on main untouched.

options.description: Pick Other and paste the two repo URLs (one of yours, or the friend's if it is public).

# Throwaway: start a Next.js server (dev or start), POST weak spots, restart, GET them back.
param([string]$Mode = "dev", [int]$Port = 3100)

$repo = "C:\Users\Home\Desktop\open-source\Personal-viva"
$url = "http://localhost:$Port/api/spike-memory"

function Start-Server {
  $p = Start-Process -FilePath "pnpm.cmd" -ArgumentList $Mode, "--port", $Port -WorkingDirectory $repo -PassThru -WindowStyle Hidden `
    -RedirectStandardOutput "$env:TEMP\viva-next-$Mode.log" -RedirectStandardError "$env:TEMP\viva-next-$Mode.err"
  foreach ($i in 1..40) {
    try { Invoke-WebRequest -Uri "http://localhost:$Port" -UseBasicParsing -TimeoutSec 5 | Out-Null; return $p } catch { Start-Sleep -Seconds 2 }
  }
  throw "server did not start"
}

function Stop-Server {
  Get-CimInstance Win32_Process -Filter "Name='node.exe'" |
    Where-Object { $_.CommandLine -like "*Personal-viva*" -and $_.CommandLine -like "*next*" } |
    ForEach-Object { Stop-Process -Id $_.ProcessId -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }
  Start-Sleep -Seconds 2
}

$id = "spike-$Mode-" + (Get-Date -Format "HHmmss")
Start-Server | Out-Null
$body = @{ repoId = $id; weakSpots = @("JWT refresh flow", "database indexes") } | ConvertTo-Json
"[$Mode] POST: " + (Invoke-RestMethod -Uri $url -Method Post -Body $body -ContentType "application/json" | ConvertTo-Json -Compress)
Stop-Server
Start-Server | Out-Null
"[$Mode] GET after restart: " + (Invoke-RestMethod -Uri "$url`?repoId=$id" | ConvertTo-Json -Compress -Depth 5)
Stop-Server

input.new_string:
### Mastra spike (task 0.4, measured 4 Oct 2026 with `scripts/spikes/mastra.ts`)

- **D24. Native tool calls stay in the agent.** `readFile` was called in 5 of 5 runs on hosted 26B (median 2.9 s) and 1 of 1 on local `gemma4:e4b` (85 s). No need to drive tools from deterministic code.
- **D25. Structured output uses the schema-in-prompt mode** (`structuredOutput: { schema, jsonPromptInjection: true }`), then zod. Reason: Google's native JSON-schema mode hung with no response in 4 of 15 calls (each hang lasted about 308 s before a retry succeeded, or hit our 30 s timeout), while schema-in-prompt passed 5 of 5 in the spike and 10 of 10 in the benchmark at 3 to 7 s. Small samples; Phase 1 evals will re-measure.
- **D26. Every hosted model call gets a timeout** (`abortSignal: AbortSignal.timeout(30_000)`) plus one retry. `[WHY]` Without it a silent hang lasts 5 minutes, which is Node's default fetch timeout.
- **D27. Local model wiring:** `model: { id: "ollama/gemma4:e4b", url: OLLAMA_BASE_URL }` works through Mastra's router (Ollama's OpenAI-compatible endpoint). All four checks passed 1 of 1, in 50 s, 85 s, 210 s and 544 s.
- **D28. Memory:** `@mastra/memory` + `LibSQLStore` with an absolute `file:` path works inside a Next.js route handler under `next dev` and under `next build` + `next start`; a value saved before a server restart was read back after it. Weak spots are stored by plain code as thread metadata (one thread per repo), not by the model. `@libsql/client` is already on Next.js's built-in external-packages list; our `serverExternalPackages` entry is a belt-and-braces duplicate.
- **D29. Dynamic paths in routes need `/*turbopackIgnore: true*/`** inside `path.resolve(...)`, otherwise the production build warns that it is tracing the whole project.

Thinking could not be switched off on the OpenAI-compatible URL (`reasoning_effort` returned HTTP 400 "not supported for this model") and the thoughts came back inside the answer as `<thought>` text.

Three of them sat for about 308 s (Node's default fetch timeout is 300 s) before the SDK's retry succeeded, so the check still "passed" and the median still read 2 s. - **How it works (Phase 0, plain language):**
  - The app is a Next.js project. Nothing user-facing exists yet; Phase 0 only proved the risky parts.
  - A Mastra "agent" is a wrapper around a model plus tools. We give it a model address: Google's hosted Gemma 4 26B by default, or the Gemma running in Ollama on the laptop. Swapping is one env variable.
  - A "tool" is a normal TypeScript function the model may ask to run (here `readFile`). Gemma decides when to call it; our code does the reading.
  - For structured answers we describe the JSON shape in the prompt, then check the reply with a zod schema. If the shape is wrong, the code knows immediately instead of crashing later.
  - Memory is a small SQLite-style file (`.viva/memory.db`) written by plain code through Mastra's memory API; it survives restarts.
  - Entire saves each coding session as a git ref next to the commit it produced. Viva will read those refs to learn which files the agent wrote and what it was asked to do.
